tour.name: Jerash & Amman Private Tour: the Roman City of Gerasa, the Citadel & the Roman Theatre
tour.subtitle: Roman Jordan in one private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the colonnaded streets, Oval Plaza and temples of Jerash, one of the best-preserved Roman cities outside Italy, Ajloun Castle, and in Amman the Citadel with the Temple of Hercules, the Roman theatre and the old souks.

tour.overview:
Jerash, ancient Gerasa, was one of the cities of the Decapolis and flourished under Roman rule, especially in the 2nd century AD. Buried by sand after earthquakes, it is one of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities in the world, with colonnaded streets, temples, theatres and an oval plaza. Amman, the capital of Jordan, was the Roman Philadelphia, and its Citadel hill has been inhabited for millennia.

This private day shows Roman and Islamic Jordan with a licensed guide and a vehicle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Amman
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate

WHAT YOU SEE
• Jerash.
• Ajloun Castle.
• The Amman Citadel.
• The Roman theatre.
• Downtown Amman.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide brings the Roman city to life, and the vehicle links Jerash, Ajloun and Amman in one comfortable day.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, families and first-time visitors.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the Dead Sea and biblical sites, choose our Madaba, Mount Nebo and Dead Sea tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Jerash is about 50 minutes from Amman. The Roman Army and Chariot Experience, a re-enactment, runs some days.

days.name: Jerash, Ajloun Castle, the Amman Citadel, the Roman theatre and downtown
days.description:
What to expect: Roman Jerash and the history of Amman, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive north to Jerash. You enter through Hadrian's Arch, built to honour the emperor's visit in 129 AD, pass the hippodrome and reach the Oval Plaza, surrounded by 56 Ionic columns. You walk the Cardo, the main street still paved with its original stones marked by chariot wheels, see the nymphaeum fountain, the Temple of Artemis with its tall columns, and the South Theatre, where a piper may play to show its acoustics.

After lunch, you drive into the hills to Ajloun Castle, built in 1184 by a general of Saladin to control the iron mines and defend against the Crusaders, with views over the Jordan Valley. Back in Amman, you visit the Citadel, with the giant columns of the Temple of Hercules, the Umayyad Palace and the Jordan Archaeological Museum, then descend to the Roman theatre, with seats for some 6,000 spectators, and walk through the downtown souks for knafeh, the warm cheese pastry, before returning to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Amman.
09:30 – Jerash.
12:30 – Lunch.
13:30 – Ajloun Castle.
15:15 – Amman Citadel.
16:15 – Roman theatre and souks.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Roman Army and Chariot Experience can be added on days it runs.
• Rainbow Street is lovely in the evening.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are entrances included?
faq.answer: Yes, or deducted if you have the Jordan Pass.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Jerash is large and uneven; the main areas are reachable at a slow pace.

faq.question: Can we skip Ajloun?
faq.answer: Yes, and spend more time in Amman instead.

faq.question: Is Amman safe?
faq.answer: Yes, Amman is safe and welcoming.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Can we combine Jerash with the Dead Sea?
What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, a hat, sun protection and modest clothes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November; the Jerash Festival runs in summer.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Jordan: guides and drivers appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
